newsitem.title: UK: London palladium fixed at $160.25, new 21-mth high.
newsitem.headline: London palladium fixed at $160.25, new 21-mth high.

text.p: The price of palladium fixed at a new 21-month high of $160.25 per ounce on Thursday, up $3.25 from the previous fix.
The price is the highest since June 28, 1995 when it stood at $160.85.
The rare white metal, used mainly in autocatalysts and electronics, has risen 40 percent since it plummeted to a 43-month low of $114.25 in late last November.
Fuelling the market are delays in talks between Russia, the world's biggest supplier and leading importer Japan to negotiate sale contracts for 1997.

"It's important to remember that this is not a reflection of the absolute level of Russian stocks. It's about the availability of these stocks," said Andy Smith, precious metals analyst at Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS).
Russia's former economy minister Yevgeny Yasin said on Thursday there was no reason for panic in the palladium market.

But a Russian trade representative in Japan said earlier this week that there would be no shipments in April and possibly none in May since the state export agency Almaz had yet to receive export quotas for this year.
Analysts say even if talks between Russia and Japan resume now, it would take a month for shipments to begin.
Shipments ceased in November last year and Almaz has been waiting for export licences to be signed by the Russian prime minister ever since.
